items.title: **UTC-midnight arrival timezone artifact** in server-side weather path
items.evidence: Server-side `parseTripDate` helper added at [server/src/utils/dates.ts](server/src/utils/dates.ts), mirroring [client/src/utils/dates.ts:56-84](client/src/utils/dates.ts) verbatim (extract UTC y/m/d, rebuild as local noon on the same calendar day — local accessors then read the stored UTC day regardless of process TZ). items.title: **Drive-day count uses cap + grace** — the daily limit is a guideline with a give-or-take, not a wall
items.evidence: Benny 2026-09-05: "the drive time is a guideline, not set in stone." [planLegSplits](server/src/controllers/trips.ts) already kept a single leg as one day up to cap + LEG_GRACE_HOURS (1.0 h) but counted DAYS at the bare cap, so a 12.7 h drive at a 6 h cap became three 4.2 h days and 'two nights to Del Rio' was a fight. Now days = ceil(hours / (cap + grace)) and a placed sub-leg is accepted up to cap + grace + tolerance — two 6.4 h days. items.title: **Map click-to-popup centering** — pan camera so clicked stop's popup is fully visible
items.evidence: `focusStop` useCallback in [client/src/pages/trips/TripMapPage.tsx](client/src/pages/trips/TripMapPage.tsx) wraps `setSelectedStop` + `mapInstance.panTo({ lat, lng })` + `mapInstance.panBy(0, -offset)`. Wired at the three click sites: marker `addListener('click', …)`, sidebar row `onClick`, and sidebar row `onKeyDown` (Enter/Space). The `setSelectedStop` calls in `handleUpdateNights` (nights stepper) and the popup close button are deliberately left as raw state updates — they don't need a camera move. The popup is an `<OverlayViewF>` geographically anchored to the stop, so without a camera move sidebar-list clicks on off-screen stops produced no visible feedback (popup rendered outside the viewport) and clicks on markers near map edges clipped the ~260px popup card above the marker. **History — sign and magnitude correction:** the initial fix passed `panBy(0, +offset)` with `offset = clamp(80, mapH/3.5, 160)`. The sign was inverted (Google's `panBy` +y moves the map *center* south, which makes markers appear to move *north* on screen — the previous fix was nudging clicked markers into the upper third instead of the lower third, so the Crested Butte case clipped the popup off the top edge instead of fixing it). Tightened to: `NEEDED_CLEARANCE_PX = 296 (full-variant card) + 36 (triangle gap) + 24 (breathing) = 356`; `offset = min(max(NEEDED_CLEARANCE_PX - mapH/2, 80), mapH * 0.3)`; `panBy(0, -offset)`. On a 550px desktop map: offset=81, marker lands at y=356, clearance above ≈ 356 (fits full-variant popup with 24px breathing). On a 340px mobile map: offset caps at 102, marker lands at y=272, full-variant popup clips by ~60px at top in worst case (mathematically unavoidable on small mobile + maximum content) but marker stays visible — typical content fits cleanly. Already-centered clicks get a modest ~80px downward nudge that keeps the popup top unclipped. First-load races (mapInstance null) safely no-op via the `if (mapInstance && …)` guard.

items.title: **OHV/off-road destinations: own data source**
items.evidence: Data-source ceiling, not a bug. The OHV Destinations page uses Rec.gov/RIDB, which does NOT index most Forest Service / BLM OHV areas. Live probe near Tonto NF (Phoenix area, ~33.8/-111.4) confirmed the real riding areas — Bulldog Canyon, St. Clair, Sycamore — are absent from RIDB entirely (0 hits each); only 1 OHV-tagged facility (Desert Vista OHV Area) was within range, so users in prime OHV country get a near-empty page. NOT fixable by widening the radius (RIDB caps `radius` ~50mi and `TOTAL_COUNT` did not grow across 25/50/100/150mi in the probe) or by filter changes (the areas simply aren't in the dataset).
items.whatRemains: **Fix (real one):** build our own OHV dataset by ingesting authoritative FREE/public-domain government GIS feeds into our own DB on a scheduled refresh — (a) USFS MVUM (Motor Vehicle Use Map): queryable ArcGIS feature service, GeoJSON/CSV/Shapefile, carries vehicle-type + season-of-use; covers the Forest Service areas Rec.gov misses; (b) BLM OHV data (GIS feature services; BLM/NOHVCC national OHV mapping series w/ amenities, season, camping availability); (c) AZ state OHV program data (other states later). **Hard part:** geospatial normalization — MVUM/BLM data is trails/routes (lines) and areas (polygons), not tidy lat/lng points, so deriving a representative point + name + distance for our destination-card model is the real work (the scheduled-refresh job is the easy part). **Freshness caveat:** sources update ~annually (not weekly) and don't capture temporary fire/seasonal closures, so framing stays "designated OHV areas," not "open today." **First step when picked up:** a single-source POC (USFS MVUM or BLM) for the Phoenix/Tonto region — prove the geometry→card normalization yields useful cards before building the full multi-source pipeline. **Priority:** post-launch — high value (fixes the feature for the core off-road audience) but a substantial standalone project (geospatial ingestion + multi-source normalization + new DB layer).
